notes.title: DEV NEWS: Step into the Abyss - story teaser
notes.content:
[b]The first month of 2025 has come to an end, and we are gradually moving away from the holiday season and diving into productive work.[/b]

In our New Year’s post, we already mentioned that we are transitioning to a new phase—integrating new systems to replace the old ones that were breaking the game. While this process is relatively simple in concept, it is incredibly time-consuming and monotonous. Right now, we are in the thick of it. Additionally, our artist has slightly reworked the design and appearance of the dialogue interface to better align with the overall visual style of the game.

And yes, of course, we have something to share with you. Today, we’ll show you a small snippet from the opening cutscene, offering a brief glimpse into the past of our protagonist, [b]Chris Mori. [/b]Let me emphasize once again—this is just a tiny piece of the bigger picture, meant to introduce the player to the story. At the same time, it gives a partial preview of the updated interface.

One more small, not particularly significant, but still pleasant update: while part of our team was focused on integrating the new system into the game's backend, another part was working on updating our website, which will be launching in just a few days. It may not be the most critical update, but it reflects our commitment and the seriousness of our plans.

[b][i]«I remember the day when the Emperor's troops first marched through the city in a triumphant parade. Back then, we had no idea where the world was heading.»[/i][/b] — [u][i]Notes of an unknown journalist.[/i][/u]

notes.title: Step into the Abyss - The Morality Police.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44972899/bce6ac95431a39fc524802467b2eae26aac7704a.png[/img]

Today, we decided to tell you about one of the most important institutions in our world of [b]Absorbium[/b] – the Morality Police. This is the very body without which our dystopian world could not function. Below are a few historical notes that the player will have to find in the game.

"[i]The Morality Police was established by an imperial decree in 2020, exactly one month before the expansion across the continent began. Back then, we didn’t yet call him the Emperor, and our country maintained the illusion of a democratic state. Some of us suspected where things were heading, but simple human naivety, faith in the best, and the propaganda machine denied everything. By the time we realized the truth, it was too late – war had engulfed the continent, and the Morality Police had gained enough power to destroy all dissenters.[/i]" – Unknown journalist, excerpt from the newspaper "My Struggle," dated 08.09.2023.

"[i]It has been a year since our brave Morality Police began their work. During this year, they have prevented numerous terrorist attacks and punished hundreds of dissenters—those who threatened our statehood and the Emperor's authority. The head of the Morality Police, in an interview with our journalist, asked to remind everyone that all their work is aimed at protecting ordinary citizens. Every day, hundreds of Morality Police officers risk their lives so that we can sleep peacefully. Glory to the Emperor![/i]" - Excerpt from the newspaper "Imperial Grandeur," dated 03.21.2021

"[i]They came for him at night, asking him persistently about some post in the social network 'Law'. He kept shouting that it was true, that he had just written what he thought and what was real. For three hours, I heard blows and screams – they were torturing them. Then, everything went silent, complete silence with no sound. I think it's needless to say that I never saw them again.[/i]" – Transcript of a radio broadcast from the pirate radio station "Free Citizen."

"[i]No one ever doubted that the old cartilage who loves to call himself by the menacing title of Emperor created the Morality Police solely to protect his fragile reputation. They never protected anyone except the Emperor and his interests. Their methods were primitive – torture, beatings, abductions, murders, blackmail. My friends, freedom-loving people, tried to resist, but they were foolish and didn't want to fight for real – just angry posts and peaceful protests – they were doomed to fail. They were simply caught one by one and killed. Witnesses said they didn’t shy away from torturing children to extract retractions and false statements of support for the Emperor.[/i]" – Note from an "Unknown Publicist."

In [b]Step into the Abyss[/b], as with most of the rules and aspects, we will only outline the basics; the details you will have to discover on your own. By finding and studying small fragments of the history that has happened and continues to unfold in the world of [b]Absorbium[/b], you, as a player, should experience a sense of involvement akin to reality, where you have to learn about events unfolding every day. However, this won’t be mandatory, and you will be able to complete the game without delving into its history.

notes.title: Demonstration of the Dialogue System - Step into the Abyss
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=bI6oseL_sM0;full][/previewyoutube]

We've been thinking, and we realized that we've been showing you a lot of screenshots but very few video demonstrations of what we're working on. Today, we want to correct this oversight and, following up on our previous demonstration of the dialogue system interface, show it to you in full on video. This is just a small, insignificant snippet of one of the many dialogues you'll encounter in the game.

Today, besides the usual updates on what we're working on and what we're ready to show, we’d like to share with you a bit more openly. [b]Step into the Abyss[/b] is the first game for our team and our first experience in developing a complete and finished game, which is why we’ve had to delay the release a few times and decided to rework some aspects that seemed like great solutions on paper. And even though this path is thorny and challenging, we are getting better every day, overcoming difficulties, learning, and, most importantly, gaining confidence in our game idea and choices. To give you an idea of how challenging this process is for a team of four, the video you’re seeing was developed, polished, and fine-tuned over a little more than a month. But this process is what brings us all joy.

We decided to share with you this openly because we’re almost ready to show you even more gameplay from [b]Step into the Abyss,[/b] as work on the demo version is in full swing, although we’re still fixing some rough edges. Very soon, we’ll be ready to show you more gameplay and announce the much-anticipated date when you can get your hands on [b]Step into the Abyss[/b] and dive into the story of Detective Chris Mori.

notes.title: The dialogue system is the foundation of Step into the Abyss.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44972899/4282ff9d74ea1ae060cf28af4d0c7b3bf9e8503f.png[/img]
We have already indirectly touched on the topic of dialogues in our Step into the Abyss, but it was only indirect. We need to rectify this injustice. Dialogues as a system are fundamental to our game. After all, a detective's work is not only about inspecting the crime scene, collecting, and analyzing evidence, but also obtaining testimonies that people are not always ready to give immediately and honestly. Therefore, Chris will often have to press people for the truth, and the player will need to analyze the situation, compare facts, and determine whether they are being told the truth or not.

One of our main goals is to provide the player with variability in communicating with NPCs. You will always have many dialogue development options: some responses may be harmless, some may advance the investigation or bring benefits to Chris himself, but some may be fatal.

The player must always remember that they exist in an authoritarian regime, and any action or word can have consequences, not all of which are immediate. We, in turn, want to minimize our influence as creators on what happens to the player. And this does not mean that we will not guide you at all—just that we will try to do this only in the most critical places. At other times, you will be left to yourself, and only your choice will drive the plot and the further fate of Chris Mori.

In the screenshot attached to the post, you can see a piece of the dialogue interface taken from the cutscene.

notes.title: A little about filling our world, propaganda posters
notes.content:
We have often mentioned that Absorbium is a dystopian world. It is ruled by a dictatorship, with almost all power concentrated in the hands of the Emperor. In creating this world, we strive to make it as realistic as possible, so throughout our world, you will find many classic elements typical of totalitarian or authoritarian regimes.

Any dictatorial regime always relies on the propaganda machine. Its purpose is to dull the minds of citizens and create an illusion of national unity. One of its most effective methods is the use of propaganda posters.

For example, in the city, Chris will often encounter various wanted boards for dissidents or propaganda posters. We decided to accompany this post with a few such posters.

And these are just a few of the many posters we have prepared for you.

"A cruel world, a cruel state that doesn't need smart people. They sit on cardboard without a home, without income, surviving only by scavenging. They are forced to do this, they have no other way. Unfortunately, we chose this ourselves. How easily imperial slogans win the love of the crowd." - Chris Mori.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44972899/fe5090c7e0c79cfe77383d7f4f38069d203573aa.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Animation by Chris Morey for migraines
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/embed/bbIHw2ee7Lw

Previously, we have told you about migraines and shown you what the visual effect looks like. However, our testers and many of you noticed that Chris's animation does not change during an episode. The feedback was more than fair, and our artist immediately set out to correct this oversight.

So today, we decided to show you what Chris's walking animation will look like during a migraine episode. This is just a render for now, but the team is already working on implementing it into the engine.

The development process continues as we make the final adjustments and prepare a demo version for you. But soon, we will have another surprise for you, which we think you will see very soon, possibly as early as next weekend. And here's another quote that you will find in the game:

[i]"The Emperor is great! The Emperor watches! Be happy under the Emperor's gaze! For the glory of the empire!"[/i]
